title: Phased flag retirement and schema-evolution playbook for streaming, tool-calls, and structured-output
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Context: As we expand structured output contracts and function/tool-calling semantics, we introduced short-lived behavior flags to gate new behavior (streaming chunk framing, tool-call tokenization changes, and structured schema enforcement). Goal: establish a repeatable, low-friction playbook to retire these behavior flags, provide an automated migration path for customers, and create a regression test suite that guarantees backward compatibility across streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs. Scope: streaming API, function/tool calling behavior, structured-output schema enforcement, server-side warning headers, and developer-facing migration docs. Out of scope: infra-only incidents and non-API infra flags.
acceptance_criteria: A documented phased timeline for introducing deprecation warnings, opt-in windows, and flag removal is published and approved by legal/marketing.
Customer-facing migration guide with code snippets for SDKs (Python, JS, Go) exists and is linked from the API changelog.
Automated compatibility test harness covers: streaming resume/parity, tool-call invocation semantics, and structured-output schema validation; runs in CI and nightly regression.
Server emits standardized deprecation headers and dashboard alerts when users still rely on flags.
A canary cohort (internal + opt-in customers) completes verification and no P0 regressions are observed for 2 weeks before global removal.
Rollback plan and automated fallback to previous runtime variant are validated in staging and documented.
Telemetry events for migration progress and customer errors are defined and wired to Console dashboards.
SDKs and official examples updated to remove flag usage before the final removal date.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Audit (2 weeks): Inventory all live behavior flags related to streaming/tool-calls/structured outputs and map active customers and SDK usage.
Phase 1 — Opt-in Beta (3 weeks): Introduce stable behavior as opt-in with explicit flag; collect compatibility signals and error rates from canary customers.
Phase 2 — Warning Window (30 days): Keep legacy behavior as default but emit Deprecation-Warning header and console inbox messages; publish migration doc and SDK snippets.
Phase 3 — Opt-out Transitional Window (14 days): Flip default to new behavior, preserve legacy via explicit legacy_flag=true; strong logging and prioritised support for migrating customers.
Phase 4 — Removal (target date): Remove legacy codepath behind flags; roll out via staged release groups with runtime fallback for 48 hours on anomaly detection.
Phase 5 — Postmortem and Signal Review (2 weeks): Consolidate telemetry, UX feedback, and update playbook for future deprecations.
Communication: publish timeline to changelog, send targeted emails to affected accounts, and create a Console banner for customers using legacy behavior.
migration_notes: Streaming: switch from legacy framing to chunked events by setting stream_mode='new' in examples; ensure client buffer logic tolerates partial event boundaries. Example code snippets provided for Python/JS.
Tool/function calling: verify tool invocation tokens and name normalization; update call sites to use structured 'tool_call' object shape and remove reliance on legacy flat metadata fields.

Structured outputs: supply a small validation stub that runs schema checks locally using the official schema validator (link in docs) and add a tolerant parsing path to handle minor shape diffs during migration.
SDKs: upgrade to the minimum supported SDK versions listed in the guide; older SDKs will continue to work during the warning window but will be unsupported after removal.
If you rely on the legacy flag and cannot migrate within the timeline, contact support to request a temporary extension and access to a dedicated migration engineer.
test_plan: Unit tests for serialization/parsing of streaming frames and structured payloads.
End-to-end CI job that spins up runtime variants (legacy/new) and exercises: streaming resume behavior, tool-call roundtrip accuracy, and schema enforcement edge cases.
Load tests to confirm that new batching/streaming framing does not regress p99 latency under representative traffic patterns.
Compatibility matrix tests that combine SDK versions (3 permutations) with runtime variants (legacy/new) and model families (2 permutations).
Golden-file regression for structured outputs sampled from real prompt sets to capture subtle format changes.
Automated canary tests that run against opt-in customers to capture real-world signals for 2 weeks prior to removal.
Alerts: define SLO-based thresholds that trigger automatic rollback if error-rate or latency exceeds pre-defined bounds during rollout.
